title: Interactive HPC and the LUNARC Desktop Environment
problem: Enabling interactive access to HPC resources for users who need real-time feedback for visualization and exploratory computing. The challenge is providing both hardware-accelerated graphics applications and Jupyter notebooks while efficiently managing submissions to backend cluster resources.
motivation: Interactive HPC access allows researchers to iterate and explore results in real-time while leveraging expensive HPC hardware infrastructure.
method: The system pairs Cendio's ThinLinc (remote desktop software that streams graphics and user input over the network) with a custom scheduling framework called GfxLauncher. When users connect to a remote desktop, they can run graphics-accelerated applications in real time or submit Jupyter notebooks to the cluster. ThinLinc relays the graphics to the user's screen and captures their keyboard and mouse commands, while GfxLauncher manages the execution of graphics-accelerated applications and schedules notebook jobs on the cluster.
key_novelty: Combining Cendio's ThinLinc remote desktop with a custom GfxLauncher backend framework enables interactive graphics applications and Jupyter notebook access to HPC clusters.
contributions: Remote desktop-based interactive HPC environment architecture combining ThinLinc and custom backend framework
GfxLauncher framework for managing hardware-accelerated graphics applications on HPC clusters
Support for interactive Jupyter notebooks submitted to HPC cluster backends
13+ years of validated operational experience with interactive HPC access model
limitations: Specific performance metrics, scalability analysis, and architectural tradeoffs not discussed.
primary_theme: Interactive remote HPC access via desktop virtualization
